maya: Heads-up — fjord13b (int4) canary is hitting warmstart OOMs on hostpool-7.
maya: Seen ~12% OOMs over the last 2 hours during canary traffic (small prompts). stack trace points to KV alloc while generating prefix.
maya: paste of the relevant log:
```
[2026-03-22T18:12:03Z] OOM when allocating 1.2GiB for kv_cache shard 3
model=fjord13b-int4 host=hp-7 slot=3 max_new_tokens=512 prefetch=8
trace: runtime.alloc -> kv_cache.grow -> memcpy -> OOM
```
maya: Also noticed latency spikes when the worker is under low burst load.

devon: ugh. is this during coldstart or just warmstart? any pattern with prompt length?
maya: mostly warmstart (KV reconstruction after eviction). small prompts but many sessions with multi-turn history. seems kv cache grows back to full size and memory gets fragmented.
sam: quick ideas — lower default max_new_tokens for this model, reduce prefetch window, and enable soft-reserve for canary nodes. also try microbatching vs big batch.
maya: proposed quick patch I tested locally:
```
model_defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  prefetch: 4
  max_batch_size: 4
  kv_evict_threshold: 0.65
  soft_reserve: true
```
sam: nice. lowering max_new_tokens halves the peak allocation in many cases. prefetch 4 also reduced concurrent KV warm allocations.
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary deploy 6189991234 -> fjord13b-int4 patch v2 started. link: https://console.redwood/models/fjord13b/canaries/6189991234
luis: ran quick A/B on canary v1 vs v2 for 30m: OOM rate v1=11.8%, v2=0.9%. p95 latency improved 120ms -> 90ms. cost per request ~ -4%.
luis: caveat: quality eval on our 1k prompt set shows small regression on extremely long rollups (>2k tokens) — sam/aya can we add a targeted eval? @sam
sam: yes I'll add an eval job to the pipeline to check hallucination/length truncation cases. if regression is only on >2k we can gate the max_new_tokens by model annotation or route long calls to a high-mem pool.
maya: operational plan: roll this patch out to dedicated canaries, monitor OOM rate, latency, and our quality checks for a day. if OOM <1% and quality diffs < 0.5% we'll promote to stable.
devon: follow-up: we should add a runtime metric for kv_alloc_peak and slab_frag_ratio, and alert at kv_alloc_peak > 900MiB on fjord13b hosts.
maya: created ticket infra#3421 for metrics + alert, and PR #826 to update model defaults. linking here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3421
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary deploy v2 succeeded on 3/3 hosts. Monitoring window will remain open for 24h.
maya: thanks team — I'll keep the thread updated if anything pops. :thumbsup:
